title: Runtime layers beyond the cockpit
intro: Preloop and OpenRouter remain useful separate planes, not the Codex runtime itself: Preloop for policy/audit and PR review flows, OpenRouter when an external workflow needs deliberate multi-model routing. The cockpit migration made that boundary clearer.
stance: Runtime controls sit under human Priority 0 (P0) gates — send, secrets, irreversible publish. A policy firewall is not consent. A PR review bot is not a merge button.

preloop.title: Preloop
preloop.lede: Preloop is an optional policy and audit plane for agent tool use and Cloud review flows. It layers under host controls and human gates — it does not replace Codex sandboxing/permissions, send approval, secrets-out-of-chat, or git fail-closed.
practices: Treat Preloop as a runtime companion for selected MCP/tool audit and Cloud flows — not as the only safety system.
Keep human gates for irreversible outbound and secret handling; Preloop adds another inspection layer.
Prefer lean builtins for approvals; do not let policy tooling become a second always-on essay.
Keep enrollment tokens and local Preloop config secrets out of skills and chat.
not: Not a substitute for Priority 0 (P0) send-gates or secrets capture dialogs.
Not a reason to auto-approve destructive shell or publish actions.
Not a place to store API tokens in the harness tree.

openrouter.title: OpenRouter
openrouter.lede: Model access depends on the host configuration. Codex and Cursor can use their native/default model access; a separately configured gateway can serve selected external workflows. OpenRouter provides multi-provider routing and fallbacks where deliberately configured, including some review workflows. It is not a universal path for the cockpit.
practices: Separate model choice (which model answers) from provider choice (who serves it).
Choose a model available to the execution credential, then prove repository checkout, tool execution, and structured result capture end to end.
Use provider failover for uptime; use explicit model fallback lists when you accept a different model answering.
Keep API keys in Bitwarden Secrets Manager — never in chat or skills.
Measure comfort vs cost: routing flexibility is not an excuse to skip proof class.
not: Not a replacement for skills/rules/memory — it is transport for model calls.
Not proof that a host session uses this route; check that host’s configuration.
Not “set and forget” for data-retention or ZDR choices; configure deliberately when it matters.
Not a productivity multiplier claim by itself.

prChecks.title: PR / commit checks
prChecks.lede: On product repos I wire Preloop Cloud as a pull-request reviewer and OpenRouter as the model path behind it. The point is shift-left: catch semantic issues on the commit before self-hosted CI eats the afternoon.

steps.title: Push the PR commit
steps.body: Before a push, confirm the human has authorised that repository, content and action and that required checks pass. Where action-bound verification is required, the executor must verify it at execution time. A review pass alone is not permission.

steps.title: Preloop reviewer runs
steps.body: A Preloop Cloud pull-request reviewer flow looks at the change set. Models are reached through OpenRouter (first-class routing on the Preloop gateway — not a one-off script in the repo).

steps.title: Commit status posts
steps.body: Preloop posts a GitHub commit status (context `preloop`) — pass / fail / pending — against that SHA. Comments or findings can land on the PR as well.

steps.title: CI can wait (optional gate)
steps.body: GitHub Actions that burn self-hosted runners can wait for that `preloop` status before starting. Flip the gate on when you want ordering; leave reviews async when you only want the signal.

practices: The human owns the merge decision. An agent can execute a specifically authorised merge within scope after the required checks. A Preloop status supplies review evidence, not merge authority.
Keep OpenRouter keys in Bitwarden Secrets Manager (or the vault Preloop Cloud uses); never in workflow YAML or chat.
Prefer async review by default; make CI wait only when runner time is scarce or the failure mode is expensive.
When the gate is on, fix or skip with an explicit, rare bypass — do not normalise “ignore Preloop”.
Keep desktop tool audit, Codex host controls, and the GitHub PR-reviewer flow mentally separate — related safeguards, different planes.
not: Not a replacement for unit tests, hardware proof, or Bugbot / human review.
Not a reason to paste secrets into GitHub Actions logs “so the reviewer can see them”.
Not the same thing as Preloop’s desktop MCP approvals in Cursor.

together: The durable harness — portable skills, explicit policy, memory, signed patterns, gates and proof — supports the working relationship. Codex owns its model path, sandbox and permissions; those host-native mechanisms are dependencies and adapters, not portable assets. Preloop can audit selected tool flows and review PR commits; OpenRouter routes external model capacity for those workflows. CI may wait on the review signal. Humans still own consequential actions and merges.
summary: The harness supports the work through procedures, evidence and controls. Guidance files do not install enforcement. Host configuration determines model access and permissions; optional services cover only their configured flows. Human decisions remain necessary for consequential actions, even when an agent performs the authorised execution.
